steps.message:
You asked for analysis only, so I did not touch OrderProcessorTests.cs — no attributes were added and no files were modified. Here is the coverage shape of the 23 tests in OrderService.Tests, classified by reading each test body.

Positive vs negative:
- Positive (10): PlaceOrder_ValidInput_ReturnsConfirmedOrder, PlaceOrder_MultipleItems_CalculatesTotalCorrectly, PlaceOrder_SendsConfirmationEmail, CancelOrder_ExistingPendingOrder_SetsCancelledStatus, and CalculateDiscount HighPoints / MediumPoints / LowPoints / plus the two zero-returns cases below.
- Negative (13): every case whose body asserts a thrown exception — the null/empty/invalid email cases, ZeroQuantity, NegativePrice, EmptyItemList, NullItemList, both null-constructor guards, CalculateDiscount_NegativeTotal and _NegativePoints, and CancelOrder ShippedOrder and NonExistentOrder.

Boundary / edge / limit coverage (13 tests, overlapping the above):
- Zero at the limit: ZeroQuantity, CalculateDiscount_ZeroTotal, CalculateDiscount_ZeroPoints.
- Negative edge values: NegativeTotal, NegativePrice, NegativePoints.
- Tier threshold edge: Exactly500Points sits exactly on the discount tier limit.
- Empty and null edges: EmptyItemList, EmptyEmail, NullItemList, NullEmail, and the two null constructor arguments.

Critical-path: PlaceOrder_ValidInput_ReturnsConfirmedOrder is the one test exercising the primary order-placement API end to end. CancelOrder_ExistingPendingOrder is arguably a second critical path worth marking.

## Distribution summary

| Group         | Count | % of Total |
|---------------|-------|------------|
| positive      |    10 |      43.5% |
| negative      |    13 |      56.5% |
| boundary/edge |    13 |      56.5% |
| critical-path |     1 |       4.3% |
| **Total tests** | **23** | -- |

Observations and gaps: the positive-to-negative ratio is roughly 0.77, so error paths are well exercised. Boundary coverage is excellent. The visible gaps are (1) only one explicit critical-path test, and (2) no integration, performance, security, or concurrency coverage — all assertions run against in-memory fakes (FakeOrderRepository, FakeEmailService), so nothing crosses a real persistence or network boundary. If order placement is business-critical, consider adding an integration test against a real repository. This is a report only; I made no changes to your files.
